newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus to scrap petrol tax after company deficits.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus to scrap petrol tax after company deficits.

text.p: Government tax on petrol companies will be slashed in Cyprus after complaints by dealers they are running up deficits from the high price of crude whilst local prices remain unchanged, sources said on Wednesday.
"A decree will be published in the official gazette on October 19," said a government source requesting anonymity.
"The additional tax imposed on petrol companies will be scrapped, effective immediately."

The additional tax, a surcharge imposed for every litre sold, was initially cut by 50 percent in July after local companies complained they were running up losses from currency fluctuations, the high price of crude and inflexible local prices.
Proceeds from the surcharge, which had been cut to four cents from eight for every litre sold, had been channelled to the electricity authority and the island's defence fund.
Under the new arrangement, a suspension of the tax altogether could save local dealers up to 1.6 or 1.7 million pounds ($3.43 million).
"There will still be a deficit of around five million pounds by the end of the year," said Takis Lefkaritis, chairman of three of Cyprus's six petroleum importing companies.
"It does not cover our loss," he told Reuters.
Petrol prices are reviewed every February and August by the Finance Ministry.
Buoyant world oil markets traded near six-year highs on Tuesday after resuming a storming bull run which has carried prices up 40 per cent in the space of four months.
London November futures for international benchmark North Sea Brent blend crude broke above 25 a barrel for the first time since the 1990/91 Gulf War after adding 88 cents on Monday.

"The prices in Cyprus have been at the same levels for several years inspite of increases in the price of crude," said Lefkaritis. "There should be an increase. There is no other way." ($= 0.46 pounds)
